Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Zimbabwe's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Wesley Madhevere and Tadiwanashe Marumani will open the innings for Zimbabwe. It will be Mark Adair to open the attack for Ireland. Off we go...
.. THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, it has been an eventful first half in the first-ever international game under lights on Zimbabwean soil. Ireland have the momentum with them thanks to a strong finish with the bat. On the other hand, Zimbabwe will still fancy themselves to gun down this total on what looks like a tricky surface. Join us back in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

As far as Zimbabwe are concerned, this has been a great fightback from them after the initial onslaught by the two Irish openers. Zimbabwe were all over the place with their lines and lengths upfront, conceding 38 runs in the first three overs. However, they were quick to assess the surface and resorted to cutters from the 4th over. As a result, the hosts were able to pull things back, especially after getting rid of Stirling and Balbirnie. Sikandar Raza led the way with three wickets in the middle phase with his variations and he was well-complemented by the rest of the batting unit. The hosts kept chipping away with wickets at regular intervals and did not allow Ireland to string any big partnerships. Although the debutant Trevor Gwandu bowled an expensive final over, Sikandar Raza will be pleased with his side's bowling effort.

Ireland finish on a high with a 20-run final over and they end up with 147 on the board! Even though this is nowhere close to the total they were aiming for at the start of the day, a late flourish from Gareth Delany has given them something to bowl for. After being inserted into bat, Andy Balbirnie came out all guns blazing and put the pressure on the Zimbabwean bowlers right from the word go and found decent support from Paul Stirling. Despite the platform laid by the two openers, no Irish batter was able to take the innings forward and lack of partnerships in the middle phase hurt them big time. Thanks to a quickfire 26-run unbeaten cameo from Gareth Delany, Ireland were able to cross 145.

Commentary.Commentary: Well-directed bumper, at the right shoulder of the batter, Paul Stirling goes for the pull but swings a bit early and misses out to get hit near his right shoulder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Trevor Gwandu to Paul Stirling, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Loses his radar as Gwandu strays down leg, Paul Stirling gets inside the line and lets the ball go through.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Trevor Gwandu to Paul Stirling, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Hat-trick of boundaries! Trevor Gwandu goes straight this time but on a length, Paul Stirling puts the dancing shoes on again and thumps it over mid on for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Trevor Gwandu to Paul Stirling, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Put away with ease! Trevor Gwandu digs it in short but this sits up nicely for the batter, over middle, Paul Stirling lets the ball come to him and pulls it in the vacant deep backward square leg region for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Trevor Gwandu to Paul Stirling, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it away this time! At the stumps, on a length, Paul Stirling advances down the track and smacks it with disdain over extra cover for his first boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Trevor Gwandu to Paul Stirling, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Length delivery, outside off, Paul Stirling shimmies down the track to go through the off side but mistimes his shot towards mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Trevor Gwandu to Paul Stirling, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off on a back of a length, shaping away, outside off, Paul Stirling throws his hands at the delivery but the ball does not rise and sneaks under the bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Trevor Gwandu to Paul Stirling, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Trevor Gwandu comes into the attack now.
Beauty to end the over! Serves it a bit fuller this time, outside off, enough away movement, Andy Balbirnie has a feel for the delivery without much foot movement and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Blessing Muzarabani to Andy Balbirnie, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the corridor of uncertainty, on a good length, Andy Balbirnie punches off the back foot but without much timing towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Blessing Muzarabani to Andy Balbirnie, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Flayed away for the first maximum! Blessing Muzarabani bowls it way too wide outside off, on a length, Andy Balbirnie latches onto the width as he carves it over point and clears the fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Blessing Muzarabani to Andy Balbirnie, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Much better from Muzarabani! Bends his back and digs it in short, around off, Andy Balbirnie gets on his toes to punch it through the off side but the ball jags back in to beat him on the inside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Blessing Muzarabani to Andy Balbirnie, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Short and punished! Blessing Muzarabani bowls it way too short and offers width outside off, Andy Balbirnie stands tall and frees his arms to slap it over cover-point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Blessing Muzarabani to Andy Balbirnie, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Begins on a good length, in the channel on off, Paul Stirling gets on the front foot to defend but the ball moves back in a touch. Stirling gets an inside onto the front pad and the ball rolls in front of cover for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Blessing Muzarabani to Paul Stirling, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Blessing Muzarabani.

FOUR! Lovely shot! 14 runs off the first over! Richard Ngarava errs in length again as he bowls it too full, outside off, Andy Balbirnie leans on and caresses the drive through covers for yet another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Richard Ngarava to Andy Balbirnie, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Bangs it into the deck again and at the hips, Paul Stirling misses out on the tickle as the ball thuds onto this thigh pad and rolls wide of square leg for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Richard Ngarava to Paul Stirling, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit too straight, on a back of a length, Andy Balbirnie glances it along the ground to fine leg and takes a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Richard Ngarava to Andy Balbirnie, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! This is even better! Richard Ngarava compensates by dragging his length back but strays on the pads, Andy Balbirnie stays back and tucks it with sweet timing through square leg for more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Richard Ngarava to Andy Balbirnie, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Andy Balbirnie and Ireland are underway! Overpitches this time, outside off, Andy Balbirnie does not miss out as he extends his arms and angles the bat face to guide it through covers for the first boundary of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Richard Ngarava to Andy Balbirnie, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off from over the wicket, on a length, shaping in, on middle, Andy Balbirnie hangs on the back foot and punches it with a straight bat but picks out mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Richard Ngarava to Andy Balbirnie, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now for the match to begin. Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie will open for Ireland while Richard Ngarava will begin with the ball for Zimbabwe. Let's go...

The teams and match officials are out in the middle for the respective National Anthems. We start with the anthem of Ireland followed by that of the hosts Zimbabwe. Stay tuned for the start of the game which gets underway shortly.

PITCH REPORT - Stanley Chioza is near the deck. He starts by saying that there are plenty of cracks. Mentions that it is a dry surface and teams might look to bat first. Reckons that teams would want to get a total above 180. Feels that there are cracks which might disintegrate and seamers will come into play with their cutters.

The captain of Ireland, Paul Stirling says that they were looking to bowl first as well. Adds that he is excited to play the first day-night game in Harare. Shares that the real deal starts when they play a competitive game in Zimbabwe. Ends by saying that he is really looking forward to the captaincy and with the World Cup around the corner, they want to use this game as a preparation for the mega event.

Zimbabwe's skipper, Sikandar Raza says that they will bowl first. Mentions that the reason to bowl first is due to this being the first game under lights. Shares that it takes time to settle under lights. States that it is nice to have new faces. Further adds that it has been a tough few weeks but they want to make sure that they start well. On this being the first-ever international game under lights, he says that is nice to be part of history.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Andy Balbirnie, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Mark Adair, Gareth Delany, Barry McCarthy, Craig Young, Joshua Little.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Tadiwanashe Marumani, Wesley Madhevere, Sean Williams, Sikandar Raza (C), Ryan Burl, Brian Bennett (On T20I debut), Clive Madande (WK), Luke Jongwe, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani, Trevor Gwandu (On T20I debut).
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and they have opted to BOWL first.

On the other hand, Ireland's previous T20I assignment was against India, where they suffered a series defeat at home. Despite the results not going their way, Ireland showed that they are no pushovers and have what it takes to compete with white-ball powerhouses. Having secured their berth for the 2024 T20 World Cup, newly appointed white-ball skipper Paul Stirling will be looking to kickstart their preparations for the event through this series. Other than Stirling, Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, Joshua Little, and George Dockrell will have to come good if Ireland are to register their first series win against Zimbabwe. Who will draw the first blood? Stick around to find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly...

Zimbabwe come into this T20I series on the back of their 2024 T20 World Cup Africa Region Qualifier debacle, where they missed out on qualifying for the showpiece event. As a result, Sikandar Raza and Co. have a point to prove that they are still a side not to be taken lightly. Sean Williams, Craig Ervine, Blessing Muzarabani and Ryan Burl will be required to turn up and perform for the hosts against a competitive Irish side. With a good blend of youth and experience, the Chevrons will be determined to put on a show for their fans.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of the 1st T20I between Zimbabwe and Ireland at the Harare Sports Club. The opening match of the three-match series is going to be a historic occasion, as this will be the first-ever international game to be played under lights on Zimbabwean soil. Neither side holds the edge over the other in T20Is, meaning that it is tough to gauge right now who will be lifting the silverware at the end of the third game.
... MATCH DAY ...

Cricket enthusiasts are in for a treat as Zimbabwe prepares to host Ireland in a riveting three-match T20I series, kicking off at the Harare Sports Club. Eager to bounce back from the disappointment of missing the 2024 T20 World Cup, the hosts pin their hopes on seasoned campaigners Sikandar Raza, Craig Ervine, and Sean Williams to spearhead the run-scoring. Wesley Madhevere, Tadiwanashe Marumani, ​​​​and Ryan Burl add depth to Zimbabwe's batting, with Raza's exceptional all-round contributions standing out, having claimed seven Player of the Match awards in 2023. Richard Ngarava leads the pace attack alongside Luke Jongwe, and Blessing Muzarabani, forming a well-balanced outfit geared to kickstart the series positively. On the flip side, Ireland, having secured a spot in the upcoming T20 World Cup, view this series as a crucial litmus test. Skipper Paul Stirling, a pivotal opener, partners with the in-form Andy Balbirnie at the helm. Harry Tector and Lorcan Tucker fortify the middle order, supported by dynamic all-rounders George Dockrell and Curtis Campher. The pace department is spearheaded by the experienced Joshua Little, complemented by Mark Adair and Craig Young, while Gareth Delany manages spin duties with Dockrell. The series becomes a platform for Ireland to gauge their readiness for the T20 World Cup, with a focus on strategic player assessments. As history indicates a balanced rivalry, with both teams winning six encounters each in their 12 previous meetings, anticipation builds for a closely contested battle. The Harare Sports Club sets the stage for an enthralling clash, leaving cricket enthusiasts eager to witness which team will emerge victorious in this closely matched T20I series.
